01 / Beyond the ring
01

THE FIGHT
IS NOT
THE POINT.

Boxing is the vehicle. Human development is the purpose. Every challenge becomes an opportunity to recognise, regulate, choose and take responsibility.

Body

Movement, coordination, physical capability and the courage to attempt difficult things.

Mind

Breathing, attention, emotional regulation and sound judgement under pressure.

Character

Identity, responsibility, relationships and leadership of self.

Individual first

One-to-one coaching is the starting point; carefully matched pair work may follow.

Built for the individual

Developmentally adapted practice for young people aged 4–18, subject to suitability.

Beyond training

Learning transfers into home, kura, sport, relationships and everyday decisions.

First session free

An introductory session gives the young person and whānau a chance to see whether the fit is right.

02 / The foundations

TWO TRADITIONS.
DISTINCT ROOTS.
SHARED QUESTIONS.

Stoic Code Combat draws from Māori approaches to identity and collective responsibility, and from Stoic inquiry into judgement and conduct. Their histories and meanings remain distinct.

Mātauranga Māori

Know where you stand.

Whakapapa, manaakitanga, whanaungatanga and rangatiratanga inform an approach that sees the young person within whānau, community and responsibility to others.

WHAKAPAPA · MANA · WHANAUNGATANGA
TE WHARE TAPA WHĀ · RANGATIRATANGA
Stoic philosophy

Choose how you act.

Stoic thinkers invite us to examine what is within our influence, practise courage and discipline, and measure leadership by conduct rather than title.

MARCUS AURELIUS · EPICTETUS · SENECA
JUDGEMENT · COURAGE · SELF-MASTERY
“A young person does not become a leader because we call them one. They become capable through what they repeatedly practise.”

SCC guiding principle

03 / The SCC development engine

NOT A MOMENT.
A METHOD.

A living practice of leadership: recognise what is happening, understand your position, choose deliberately, act with purpose, observe the outcome, adapt, and learn to govern yourself. These habits grow through challenge, reflection and everyday responsibility — not through a single moment of performance.

The journey reaches beyond individual performance: self-awareness develops capability; capability strengthens identity; pressure tests judgement; self-governance deepens relationships, responsibility and service to others.

01Recognise
02Understand
03Choose
04Act
05Observe
06Adapt
07Self-govern

From self-awareness to capability, identity, pressure, self-governance, relationships, responsibility and service. This is a developmental journey, not a promise of instant transformation.

Lewis Aperahama · Founder, Stoic Code Combat · Hawke's Bay, Aotearoa

SCC is a youth human-performance and leadership development programme. It is not a childcare service or a guarantee of competitive boxing outcomes.
